skill.name: when-configuring-sandbox-security-use-sandbox-configurator
skill.description: Configure Claude Code sandbox security policies for file isolation, network controls, tests, and monitoring. Review privileged commands before use.
skill.summary: Guide sandbox security setup with policy design, isolation checks, testing, and monitoring.
skill.author: DNYoussef

security_audit.summary: The skill is defensive in purpose, and many static path findings are deny-list or documentation references. However, it includes executable workflows that modify host controls, run mutable npx packages, and test sensitive files with cat. It should not be auto-installed until unsafe tests are replaced and privileged commands require explicit review.

remediation.issue: Secret-read tests can disclose protected files
remediation.suggestion: Replace real /etc/shadow and SSH key reads with mock fixtures, or redirect stdout and run only inside disposable sandboxes.
Pin claude-flow to an exact reviewed version or remove live npx calls. Document integrity verification before use.

remediation.issue: Host firewall and system policy mutation
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit root approval, add dry-run and rollback steps, and scope execution to a VM or container.

remediation.issue: External network tests use public endpoints
remediation.suggestion: Use controlled local endpoints or reserved test domains instead of relying on public blocked-domain requests.

semantic_findings.title: Unsafe Secret Read Tests Can Print Sensitive Files
semantic_findings.description: The negative tests use cat on /etc/shadow and ~/.ssh/id_rsa with stdout still visible. If isolation fails, secret contents can appear in terminal output or logs.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The commands redirect stderr only. Successful reads would emit sensitive file contents before the script prints the failure message.

semantic_findings.title: Mutable Remote Package Execution
semantic_findings.description: The workflow repeatedly runs npx claude-flow@alpha during security setup. The package version is mutable and no integrity verification is documented.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Multiple npx calls use an alpha tag rather than an exact reviewed version. That creates a clear supply-chain risk in a privileged workflow.

semantic_findings.title: Host Firewall Changes Without Isolation Guardrails
semantic_findings.description: The network script sets host iptables default DROP policies and then adds broad allow rules. No dry run, namespace isolation, or enforced rollback is shown.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The commands are explicit host-level firewall operations. The surrounding workflow does not require a container, VM, dry run, or rollback before execution.

content.value_statement: Sandbox misconfiguration can expose host files, credentials, and network services. This skill guides Claude Code, Codex, and Claude through policy design, isolation setup, testing, and monitoring.
actual_capabilities: Documents sandbox security requirements, threat models, risks, and compliance needs.
Defines file isolation policies with allowed paths, denied paths, and temporary storage limits.
Outlines network isolation with trusted domains, blocked protocols, ports, and firewall rules.
Creates example scripts for file controls, network controls, testing, and monitoring.
Builds deployment and summary documentation for sandbox security operations.
limitations: Requires careful review before any command runs with elevated privileges.
Does not prove a sandbox is secure without environment-specific testing.
Example network and filesystem rules may not match every operating system.
Some included test commands can expose sensitive data if used unchanged.

use_cases.title: Prepare Sandbox Security Controls
use_cases.description: Create requirements, threat models, and least-privilege file boundaries before enabling automated coding workflows.

use_cases.title: Review Platform Isolation Design
use_cases.description: Check network, filesystem, and resource controls before a team deploys Claude Code or Codex in shared infrastructure.

use_cases.title: Organize Compliance Evidence
use_cases.description: Collect policies, test plans, deployment notes, and monitoring summaries for audit preparation.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Sandbox Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a sandbox security plan for my Claude Code workspace. Include file boundaries, network rules, tests, and review checkpoints.

prompt_templates.title: Review File Boundaries
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my proposed sandbox file access rules. Identify risky allowed paths, missing deny paths, and safer alternatives.

prompt_templates.title: Design Network Tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a network isolation test plan for Codex and Claude Code. Avoid public blocked-domain requests and include expected evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Full Rollout
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit my sandbox rollout plan end to end. Flag privileged commands, secret exposure risks, rollback gaps, and monitoring blind spots.

output_examples.input: Plan file isolation for a shared Claude Code workspace.
output: A short threat model for host file exposure.
A reviewed allow list for workspace and tool paths.
A deny list for system, credential, device, and home directories.
A validation checklist with safe mock tests.

output_examples.input: Check whether my network sandbox rules are complete.
output: A trusted-domain review with justification for each exception.
A blocked-protocol review for unsafe services.
A test approach using controlled endpoints.
A list of rollback and monitoring requirements.

output_examples.input: Prepare deployment evidence for sandbox security controls.
output_examples.output: The response summarizes policies, test results, deployment steps, monitoring status, and unresolved risks for audit review.

best_practices: Run examples only in disposable sandboxes until reviewed.
Replace public network tests with controlled local endpoints.
Keep policies least privileged and document every exception.
anti_patterns: Running generated scripts as root without a dry run or rollback plan.
Using real credential paths as test targets in shared environments.
Treating a passing checklist as proof of complete isolation.

faq.question: Does this skill enforce sandbox security by itself?
faq.answer: No. It guides policy creation, scripts, tests, and monitoring that must be reviewed and run in your environment.

faq.question: Can it be used with Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow can guide Codex, Claude, and Claude Code, but commands need human approval.

faq.question: Does it need root access?
faq.answer: Some examples modify system policy and firewall settings, so elevated privileges may be required.

faq.question: Is it safe for production use?
faq.answer: Use only after replacing unsafe secret-read tests and validating commands in a disposable environment.

faq.question: What does it help document?
faq.answer: It helps document requirements, threat models, file boundaries, network rules, tests, deployment steps, and monitoring.

faq.question: Does it support compliance work?
faq.answer: It can organize SOC 2, GDPR, and internal control evidence, but it is not a compliance guarantee.
